title: quality-code team config (.claude/quality-code.json)
description: Documentation of the rules enforced by lib/base/config.mjs.

$schema.description: Ignored: lets an editor validate the file against this schema.

root.description: The project's folder when it is not the repository's top, like "web": the config stays at the top, every script, runner and the boundary hook work in this folder, and every other path in the config and the paths the scripts print and take are relative to it. Inside the repository: no "..", not absolute, one line.

adapter.description: playwright: a frontend project (e2e tests of screens). vitest, pytest, junit, go or dotnet: a backend project (tests of the code), run by Vitest, pytest, JUnit (Maven or Gradle), go test or dotnet test. fullstack: both in one repo; the e2e folder's specs run under Playwright, the rest under the backend runner (backend, default vitest).

backend.description: Only with adapter fullstack: the runner of the backend side.

runners.description: The project's own runner when it is not Vitest or Playwright. Its tests get the generic checks; Vitest and Playwright keep the specialized ones.

unit.description: The runner of the tests of the code (the vitest adapter, or fullstack with backend vitest): node is Node's own runner, node --test. Default vitest. Not with a pytest, junit, go or dotnet backend: they run their own tests.

e2e.description: The runner of the e2e tests of screens (the playwright adapter). Default playwright.

site.description: Your Jira site, like https://example.atlassian.net. A trailing "/" is dropped.

bugTypes.description: Issue type names (any case) written to the Bug template. Absent: any type whose name contains bug, defect, incident, problem, anomal or difett.

doneStatuses.description: Jira statuses that mean the work is finished (any case). A red /quality-code:run-* run on a ticket in one of them warns that the bug is still on the branch.

titlePrefixes.description: Title prefixes the vitest rubric credits, written without brackets and matched literally. May be [] when the team uses none: the title-prefix signal then scores 0 and is never asked for.

confluence.description: false: the team has no Confluence. No QA plan is looked for, and the QA plan is left out of the Playwright score (the rest is scaled to 100).

confluenceSpaces.description: Confluence space keys the QA-plan search is limited to (Playwright), for example ["ABC"]. Left out, the search looks in all spaces; an empty list is not allowed.

ticketsDir.description: Folder for the local ticket copies, relative to the project root and inside it (no "..", not absolute; the check is on the path text, symlinks are not resolved). One line only. Backslashes become "/", a leading "./" and a trailing "/" are dropped, so the .gitignore line is <dir>/*/raw.json.

base.description: The branch feature branches start from when origin/HEAD is not it (gitflow: "develop"). /quality-code:spec reads the changes against it; --base and a merge request's target still win.

boundaries.description: Paths a test-writing run may never write. Absent: src/, .env, .env.* and the detected CI file. dist/, node_modules/, .git/ and this config are always forbidden.

path.description: A prefix ending in / (src/), an exact file (.env), or a glob with * (one segment) and ** (any depth). Relative, no "..".

why.description: One line shown when a write is refused.

allow.description: Exceptions inside a forbidden path, for example src/**/*.spec.ts.

vitest.description: Only with adapter vitest or fullstack. How quality-code runs your Vitest specs.

match.description: Spec path pattern: a prefix ending in /, an exact path, or a glob with * and **.

config.description: Vitest config file for the specs that match.

configs.description: First match wins; none means Vitest's default config.

tsconfig.description: Project file for the type-check. Default tsconfig.json when it exists.

name.description: Unique; lower-case letters, digits and -, like "unit".

folder.description: Where the layer's specs go, ending in /. Must not be inside a forbidden boundary.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's conventions for this layer, read on top of the plugin's writing guide.

layers.description: The test folders /quality-code:spec may write in. Default: one layer, { "name": "unit", "folder": "test/" }.

threshold.description: Share of Stryker's code changes the tests must catch, in percent.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds one Stryker run may take: it reruns the tests once per code change.

stryker.description: Used only when the project has node_modules/.bin/stryker.

pytest.description: Only with adapter pytest, or fullstack with backend pytest. How quality-code runs your pytest tests.

name.description: Unique; lower-case letters, digits and -, like "unit".

folder.description: Where the layer's tests go, ending in /. Test files are written by their name even inside a code folder.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's conventions for this layer, read on top of the plugin's writing guide.

layers.description: The test folders /quality-code:spec may write in. Default: one layer, { "name": "unit", "folder": "tests/" }.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds one test process may take.

command.description: The project's own test command, when the default is wrong: a template that may hold {files} (the test files), {report} (the report file read back) and {test} (one test's name).

typeCheck.description: Optional type-check command, like "mypy {files}". Left out, Python has no type step.

junit.description: Only with adapter junit, or fullstack with backend junit. How quality-code runs your JUnit (Maven or Gradle) tests.

name.description: Unique; lower-case letters, digits and -, like "unit".

folder.description: Where the layer's tests go, ending in /. Test files are written by their name even inside a code folder.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's conventions for this layer, read on top of the plugin's writing guide.

layers.description: The test folders /quality-code:spec may write in. Default: one layer, { "name": "unit", "folder": "src/test/java/" }.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds one test process may take.

command.description: The project's own test command, when the default is wrong: a template that may hold {files} (the test files), {report} (the report file read back) and {test} (one test's name).

go.description: Only with adapter go, or fullstack with backend go. How quality-code runs your go test tests.

name.description: Unique; lower-case letters, digits and -, like "unit".

folder.description: Where the layer's tests go, ending in /. "./" is the whole repo: Go tests live beside the code. Test files are written by their name even inside a code folder.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's conventions for this layer, read on top of the plugin's writing guide.

layers.description: The test folders /quality-code:spec may write in. Default: one layer, { "name": "unit", "folder": "./" }.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds one test process may take.

command.description: The project's own test command, when the default is wrong: a template that may hold {files} (the test files), {report} (the report file read back) and {test} (one test's name).

dotnet.description: Only with adapter dotnet, or fullstack with backend dotnet. How quality-code runs your dotnet test tests.

name.description: Unique; lower-case letters, digits and -, like "unit".

folder.description: Where the layer's tests go, ending in /. Test files are written by their name even inside a code folder.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's conventions for this layer, read on top of the plugin's writing guide.

layers.description: The test folders /quality-code:spec may write in. Default: one layer, { "name": "unit", "folder": "tests/" }.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds one test process may take.

command.description: The project's own test command, when the default is wrong: a template that may hold {files} (the test files), {report} (the report file read back) and {test} (one test's name).

playwright.description: Only with adapter playwright or fullstack. How quality-code runs your Playwright specs, and where it writes new ones.

match.description: Spec path pattern: a prefix ending in /, an exact path, or a glob with * and **.

config.description: Playwright config file for the specs that match.

configs.description: First match wins; none means Playwright's default config.

projects.description: Playwright projects to run, for example ["chromium"]. Left out, every project of the config runs.

tsconfig.description: Project file for the type-check. Default tsconfig.json when it exists.

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds one Playwright process may take.

folder.description: Where /quality-code:spec puts new Playwright specs, ending in /. Must be inside your Playwright config's testDir and not inside a forbidden boundary. Default: the default config's testDir when it is a plain string, else e2e/.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's Playwright conventions (fixtures, login, which APIs to stub), read on top of the plugin's writing guide.

ungradedTitles.description: Optional regular expression (any case) for the titles of tests that never assert, such as screenshot captures ("conformance|capture"). They are neither graded nor mutated. Left out, every test is graded.

redTags.description: The tags /quality-code:spec puts on red Playwright tests (a ticket scenario's, an extra probe's), which a merge gate can skip. null: red tests get no tag.

seed.description: Optional. What /quality-code:seed reads to write a ticket's test data. Every field is optional.

builders.description: Only with adapter vitest or fullstack. The files that hold the project's own seed builders (for example test/helpers/seed.ts). /quality-code:seed calls only functions these files export. Left out, it looks for candidates and asks.

dataset.description: A .md file that documents the project's known, idempotent test dataset (rows, ids, values). /quality-code:seed prefers its values and ids over new ones.

stubsFrom.description: Only with adapter playwright or fullstack. The folder, ending in /, whose specs hold the existing route stubs (page.route ... fulfill). Response shapes are copied from them, never guessed. Left out, every spec of the project is searched.

guide.description: Optional .md file with the team's own seeding rules (foreign-key order, money formats, endpoints to stub), read by /quality-code:seed on top of the plugin's seed guide.

qaPlans.description: Optional folder, ending in /, of QA plans written as Markdown, one <feature label>.md per feature. /quality-code:spec reads the ticket's feature plan as extra rules; the ticket's Then wins. Never scored.

xray.description: Optional, Playwright and fullstack only: write XRay test cases for QA. /quality-code:spec adds one case per Playwright test it writes, /quality-code:xray writes them without tests.

csv.description: The CSV with every case, a relative path ending in .csv. Created on first use.

folder.description: Where each ticket's case.csv (and case.xlsx, when the project has exceljs) go, as <folder><KEY>/, ending in /. Default: the tickets folder.

headers.description: The header of each column, when your Xray import mapping uses other names. data is the word before a step's data in the action cell.

sides.description: Only with adapter fullstack: the title prefixes (no brackets) or labels that mark a ticket frontend, backend or fullstack. Default: FE, BE and FS. An unmarked ticket is scored for both sides.

git.description: Branch detection. Absent means detect the base from origin/HEAD, falling back to develop, main or master.

base.description: The branch merge requests target, when it differs from origin/HEAD (the repo's default branch). Wins over origin/HEAD; an explicit --base flag still wins over this.

redact.description: Name to regular expression. A redact object replaces the default, it does not add to it: keep "customerId" in it to keep customer-id redaction. customerId matches become U######, others [redacted:<name>]. E-mails and UUIDs are always redacted.

additionalProperties.description: A regular expression source. It must not match empty text.

messages.description: Texts a ticket author reads. Per rubric key (ac_present, steps, ...) any of title, missing, add, question, example, label, reject; story overrides again for Story tickets. Built-in defaults first, then messages.<key> field by field, then messages.story.<key>.

jiraFillMark.description: The line put above the sections a guided fill-in appends to the Jira description.
